32457-pioneer.title: Pioneer
32457-pioneer.creator: Unknown
32457-pioneer.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. First there was the doctor, poking around in my mouth, stabbing my eyes with a blinding beam of light, and prodding and squeezing my body. It reminded me of the day I came to live with Max and I was tempted to take a hunk out of this doctor's hand like I did the other one. But Max was there and that stopped me. I didn't want to see the hurt look that would come to his eyes every time I did something wrong.

arxiv-2103-09852.title: Quantum criticality in Ce 1-x Sm x CoIn 5
arxiv-2103-09852.creator: D. L. Kunwar, R. B. Adhikari, N. Pouse, M. B. Maple, M. Dzero, C. C. Almasan
arxiv-2103-09852.description: Abstract Motivated by the possibility of observing the co-existence between magnetism and unconventional superconductivity in heavy-fermion Ce 1-x Sm x CoIn 5 alloys, we studied how the samarium substitution on the cerium site affects the magnetic field-tuned-quantum criticality of stoicheometric CeCoIn 5 by performing specific heat and resistivity measurements.

arxiv-2103-15804.title: Decorated Merge Trees for Persistent Topology
arxiv-2103-15804.creator: Justin Curry, Haibin Hang, Washington Mio, Tom Needham, Osman Berat Okutan
arxiv-2103-15804.description: Abstract . This paper introduces decorated merge trees (DMTs) as a novel invariant for persistent spaces. DMTs combine both π 0 \pi_{0} and H n H_{n} information into a single data structure that distinguishes filtrations that merge trees and persistent homology cannot distinguish alone.

arxiv-2104-03695.title: Stabilization of Qubit Relaxation Rates by Frequency Modulation
arxiv-2104-03695.creator: Shlomi Matityahu, Alexander Shnirman, Moshe Schechter
arxiv-2104-03695.description: Abstract Temporal, spectral, and sample-to-sample fluctuations in coherence properties of qubits form an outstanding challenge for the development of upscaled fault-tolerant quantum computers. A ubiquitous source for these fluctuations in superconducting qubits is a set of atomic-scale defects with a two-level structure. Here we propose a way to mitigate these fluctuations and stabilize the qubit performance.

arxiv-2201-01116.title: Effects of neutron-skin thickness on direct hard photon emission from reactions induced by the neutron-rich projectile 50 Ca
arxiv-2201-01116.creator: S. S. Wang(王闪闪), Y. G. Ma(马余刚), D. Q. Fang(方德清), X. G. Cao(曹喜光)
arxiv-2201-01116.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by S. S. Wang(王闪闪), Y. G. Ma(马余刚), D. Q. Fang(方德清), X. G. Cao(曹喜光). Direct hard photon emissions from incoherent proton-neutron bremsstrahlung in collisions of the neutron-rich projectile 50 Ca with 12 C and 40 Ca targets are simulated in the framework of the isospin-dependent quantum molecular dynamics (IQMD) model.

arxiv-2307-03265.title: Mach number and wall thermal boundary condition effects on near-wall compressible turbulence
arxiv-2307-03265.creator: Akanksha Baranwal 1, Diego A. Donzis 1, and Rodney D. W. Bowersox 1
arxiv-2307-03265.description: Abstract We investigate the effects of thermal boundary conditions and Mach number on turbulence close to walls. In particular, we study the near-wall asymptotic behavior for adiabatic and pseudo-adiabatic walls, and compare to the asymptotic behavior recently found near isothermal cold walls ( Baranwal et al. 2022 ).

arxiv-2403-02665.title: DGAP: Efficient Dynamic Graph Analysis on Persistent Memory
arxiv-2403-02665.creator: Abdullah Al Raqibul Islam, Dong Dai
arxiv-2403-02665.description: Abstract . Dynamic graphs, featuring continuously updated vertices and edges, have grown in importance for numerous real-world applications. To accommodate this, graph frameworks, particularly their internal data structures, must support both persistent graph updates and rapid graph analysis simultaneously, leading to complex designs to orchestrate ‘fast but volatile’ and ‘persistent but slow’ storage devices.

arxiv-2406-19211.title: Numerical Analysis of the Complete Active-Space Extended Koopmans’s Theorem
arxiv-2406-19211.creator: Reza Hemmati 1,2,†,∗ , Mohammad Mostafanejad 1,2,‡,∗ , and J. V. Ortiz 3,⋆ 1 Department of Chemistry, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, Virginia 24061, USA 2 Molecular Sciences Software Institute, Blacksburg, Virginia 24060, USA 3 Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, Auburn University, Auburn, Alabama
arxiv-2406-19211.description: Abstract We investigate the numerical accuracy of the EKT ( EKT ) in reproducing the FCI ( FCI ) and CASCI ( CASCI ) IE of atomic and molecular systems calculated as the difference between the energies of N N and ( N − 1 CLOSE (N-1 ) electron states.

arxiv-2412-06915.title: Quantum phases and transitions of bosons on a comb lattice
arxiv-2412-06915.creator: Leo Radzihovsky, Emil Pellett
arxiv-2412-06915.description: Abstract Motivated to elucidate the nature of quantum phases and their criticality when entangled with a correlated quantum bath, we study interacting bosons on a “comb lattice” – a one-dimensional backbone (system) coupled at its sites to otherwise independent one-dimensional “teeth” chains (bath). We map out the corresponding phase diagram, detailing the nature of the phases and phase transitions.

arxiv-2509-15125.title: Heterotic Warm Inflation
arxiv-2509-15125.creator: Arjun Berera, Heliudson Bernardo, Suddhasattwa Brahma, Jaime Calderón-Figueroa, Rudnei O. Ramos, and Michael W. Toomey
arxiv-2509-15125.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arjun Berera, Heliudson Bernardo, Suddhasattwa Brahma, Jaime Calderón-Figueroa, Rudnei O. Ramos, and Michael W. Toomey. In this paper we propose a two-field model of warm inflation motivated from a heterotic string construction. The model contains an axion and a dilaton-like field. We show that while warm inflation can take place in the axion-field direction, thermal corrections coming from the radiation gauge fields, which couples to both the axion and the dilaton, prevent warm inflation to happen in the dilaton-field direction.

arxiv-2510-02992.title: Production of spectator neutrons, protons and light fragments on fixed targets at NICA
arxiv-2510-02992.creator: A.O. Svetlichnyi, E.Y. Vasyagina, S.D. Savenkov, I.A. Pshenichnov
arxiv-2510-02992.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by A.O. Svetlichnyi, E.Y. Vasyagina, S.D. Savenkov, I.A. Pshenichnov. The Ultrarelativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics (UrQMD) model was connected to a set of models called Ablation Monte Carlo (AMC) to identify excited spectator fragments on completion of the UrQMD modeling of nucleus-nucleus collisions and then simulate spectator decays. The UrQMD-AMC approach combines the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) clustering algorithm, which associates individual nucleons with excited clusters termed prefragments, with decay models of excited nuclei from the Geant4 toolkit.

arxiv-2510-14177.title: Reconstruction of the non-linear wave at a buoy from shoreline data and applications to the tsunami inverse problem for piece-wise sloping bathymetry
arxiv-2510-14177.creator: Oleksandr Bobrovnikov, Madison Jones, Shriya Prasanna, Josiah Smith, Alexei Rybkin, Efim Pelinovsky
arxiv-2510-14177.description: Abstract We discuss the following inverse problem: given the run-up data of a tsunami wave, can we recover its initial shape? We study this problem within the framework of the non-linear shallow water equations, a model widely used to study tsunami propagation and inundation.

arxiv-2510-26396.title: A Pragmatic View of AI Personhood
arxiv-2510-26396.creator: Joel Z. Leibo, Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets, William A. Cunningham, Stanley M. Bileschi
arxiv-2510-26396.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joel Z. Leibo, Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets, William A. Cunningham, Stanley M. Bileschi. The emergence of agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) is set to trigger a “Cambrian explosion” of new kinds of personhood. This paper proposes a pragmatic framework for navigating this diversification by treating personhood not as a metaphysical property to be discovered, but as a flexible bundle of obligations (rights and responsibilities) that societies confer upon entities for a variety of reasons, especially to solve concrete governance problems.

arxiv-2601-00425.title: Chip-scale superconducting quantum gravimeter based on a SQUID–transmon–mechanical resonator
arxiv-2601-00425.creator: Salman Sajad Wani, Mughees Ahmed Khan, Abrar Ahmed Naqash, Saif Al-Kuwari
arxiv-2601-00425.description: Abstract Precise gravitational measurements are vital for geophysics and inertial navigation, but current platforms struggle to combine absolute accuracy with high-bandwidth tracking. We address this challenge with a chip-scale superconducting gravimeter that couples a flux-tunable transmon qubit to a high- Q Q mechanical resonator. We embed the mechanical element inside the qubit’s SQUID loop.

britannica-1911-rosmini-serbati-antonio.title: Rosmini-Serbati, Antonio (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-rosmini-serbati-antonio.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-rosmini-serbati-antonio.description: Article 'Rosmini-Serbati, Antonio' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born at Rovereto in Italian Tirol on the 25th of March 1797. He belonged to a noble and wealthy family, but at an early age decided to enter the priesthood. After studying at Pavia and Padua, he took orders in 1821. In 1828 he founded a new religious order, the Institute of the Brethren of Charity, known in Italy generally as the Rosminians.

pmc-10591232.title: The Use of Free Fibula Flap in Different Extremities and Our Clinical Results
pmc-10591232.creator: Numan Atilgan
pmc-10591232.description: Background and objectivesPlastic, orthopedic, otolaryngology, and oromaxillofacial surgery specialists rely on fibula grafts to solve reconstructive problems. The aim of this study is to discuss the use and results of vascular fibula flaps in the treatment of bone and soft tissue defects in various regions with different etiologies.

pmc-11423473.creator: Jeremy H Rose, Colin J Driver, Lorna Arrol, Thomas J A Cardy, Joana Tabanez, Anna Tauro, Ricardo Fernandes, Imogen Schofield, Sophie Adamantos, Nicolas Granger, Thomas R Harcourt‐Brown

pmc-11442515.title: A fabrication strategy for millimeter-scale, self-sensing soft-rigid hybrid robots
pmc-11442515.creator: Hun Chan Lee, Nash Elder, Matthew Leal, Sarah Stantial, Elenis Vergara Martinez, Sneha Jos, Hyunje Cho, Sheila Russo
pmc-11442515.description: Soft robots typically involve manual assembly of core hardware components like actuators, sensors, and controllers. This increases fabrication time and reduces consistency, especially in small-scale soft robots. We present a scalable monolithic fabrication method for millimeter-scale soft-rigid hybrid robots, simplifying the integration of core hardware components. Actuation is provided by soft-foldable polytetrafluoroethylene film-based actuators powered by ionic fluid injection.

pmc-11714580.title: Association of High Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol with Incident Dementia in Patients with Cardiovascular Disease: Insights from a Heart‐Brain Registry
pmc-11714580.creator: Anum Saeed, Jianhui Zhu, Floyd Thoma, Oscar L Lopez, Tharick Ali Pascoal, Suresh Mulukutla, Ann D Cohen, Steven E Reis
pmc-11714580.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundLow levels of high density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL‐c) are a risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). ASCVD can increase the risk for dementia. However, the link between HDL‐C and incidence of dementia remain less clear specifically in women.

pmc-12513250.title: Unveiling photoinduced electron transfers in photosensitized polyoxometalates for solar energy conversion
pmc-12513250.creator: Christian Cariño, Anna Proust, Geoffroy Guillemot, Ludivine K/Bidi, Sébastien Blanchard, Elizabeth A. Gibson, Guillaume Izzet
pmc-12513250.description: Artificial photosynthesis faces the challenge of developing visible-light-driven strategies for converting and storing solar energy in the form of fuels and high-value chemicals. In such an approach, selective fuel production often depends on the accumulation of multiple electrons at a catalytic site.

pmc-12769640.title: Anticancer compounds from Streptomyces: insights from metagenomics and mechanistic perspective
pmc-12769640.creator: Muhanna Mohammed Al-shaibani, Noraziah Mohamad Zin, Juwairiah Remali, Nik Marzuki Sidik, Nabil Ali Al-Mekhlafi, Vanitha Mariappan, Asif Sukri
pmc-12769640.description: Cancer continues to be a leading cause of death globally, driving the ongoing search for novel bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential. Metagenomic sequencing has revolutionized this pursuit by enabling the direct detection and genomic assembly of previously uncultured Streptomyces species from environmental DNA, circumventing traditional cultivation limitations.

pmc-12963095.title: Magnetoelectric biofeedback for precision-targeted rectocele management: A randomized controlled trial of phenotype-driven pelvic floor neuromodulation
pmc-12963095.creator: Hong Zhi Geng, Chen Xu, Jiying Cong, Yuwei Li
pmc-12963095.description: PurposeMagnetoelectric biofeedback therapy (MEBFT) is an emerging intervention for moderate rectocele-associated obstructed defecation syndrome (ODS); however, its efficacy and mechanisms remain unclear. This study compared MEBFT with conventional biofeedback therapy (BFT) and developed a 3D high-resolution anorectal manometry (HR-ARM)-based predictive model for clinical decision-making.

pmc-13108112.title: Where Environment and Healthcare Meet: Air Pollution, Antibiotic Use, and Mortality in an Ageing Population in Southern Italy
pmc-13108112.creator: Caterina Elisabetta Rizzo, Roberto Venuto, Maria Gabriella Caruso, Cristina Genovese, Pasqualina Laganà
pmc-13108112.description: Background: Air pollution, antimicrobial use, and population ageing are increasingly recognised as co-occurring pressures shaping population health. This study explores their ecological association with mortality patterns in the province of Messina (Southern Italy), within a One Health-informed framework. Methods: An ecological analysis was conducted using district-by-year data (2015–2024), integrating environmental monitoring (PM10, PM2.

pmc-13116344.title: Multimodal foundation models in colorectal cancer: from prediction to trustworthy clinical insight
pmc-13116344.creator: Danial Gharaie Amirabadi, Adib Miraki Feriz, Hossein Safarpour
pmc-13116344.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by profound, multi-layered heterogeneity that limits the precision of conventional single-modality clinical tools. The emergence of multimodal foundation models (MFMs) represents a conceptual paradigm shift, moving beyond static biomarkers to capture the dynamic and evolving nature of CRC.

pmc-13288838.description: Up to 80% of diffuse midline gliomas (DMGs) are characterized by a lysine to methionine driver mutation (K27M) in the tail of histone variant H3.3, pointing to likely roles for epigenetic mechanisms in K27M-driven tumorigenesis. pmc-13441246.title: Carrier frequency of autosomal recessive monogenic disorders in the peruvian population
pmc-13441246.creator: Hugo Hernán Abarca Barriga, Flor Del Milagro Vásquez-Sotomayor, Renzo Punil Luciano
pmc-13441246.description: ObjectiveAutosomal recessive diseases represent an important group of genetic disorders whose frequency may be reduced through population screening strategies or premarital diagnosis, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where some of these conditions have personalized treatment options that are often not covered by healthcare systems.
